newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt surges on Argentina package, Mexico talk.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt surges on Argentina package, Mexico talk.

text.p: Latin American debt prices jumped on Tuesday amid optimism over Argentina fiscal package and talk that Mexico was considering another debt buyback plan, traders said.

"There was major tightening across the board," said one Brady bond trader at a U.S. money center bank, citing both investor flows and dealer-driven bullishness. "There is a lot of money floating around the market."
Argentine paper led the drive higher in the morning, as players in Buenos Aires seemed in better spirits over the prospects for the government's fiscal austerity package.
A Peronist Party parliamentary official predicted Tuesday that the Argentine Congress would pass the government's measures without major modifications.

"This has slightly changed the local mood, which had been very negative," said the chief trader at another U.S. money center bank. "Because the local mood is changing and because there are a lot of underweightings in Argentina, the shorts have to cover it."
By the end of the day, Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR rose 1-1/4 to a bid of 78, while Brazilian Cs BR8D14=RR picked up 7/8 to 64-3/4.
"The direction of least resistance is higher," said Gary Evans, senior debt strategist at Lehamn Brothers, adding that FRBs could get to 80 within two weeks.
"There are a lot of shorts out there and the technicals are very positive," he said. "The market is underallocated."

Mexican paper, which lagged in the morning, made up for lost ground on the re-emergence of rumors that the country was considering a follow-up to its successful Brady bond exchange in early May, when it swapped $2.3 billion face value of pars and discounts for fresh 30-year global bonds.

"There has been a ton of speculation about another deal similar to one they did four months ago," said one major trader, who added that he was skeptical of the rumors, particularly because of the timing.
"They have been talking about Mexican Aztecs MXFLC08=RR being called at par," the trader added. Aztecs dipped 1/4 to 98-3/4 on Tuesday.
Brazilian paper surged across the board, tightening strongly against U.S. Treasuries. One trader linked the strength to the maturation of a large options position in Brazilian EIs BRFLD06=RR.
